title: Reservation intake with smart-contract style commitments and scaling guardrails
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Introduce a reservation intake pattern that encodes throughput commitments as 'smart-contract' style agreements (machine-readable commitments) and pairs them with automated approval lanes and autoscale guardrails. Goal: reduce manual triage, accelerate onboarding for standard profiles, and ensure predictable SLOs with clear decommit and recovery paths.
context: Current flows are heavy on manual approvals and free-text SLAs. That leads to inconsistent sizing, surprise overprovisioning, and slow time-to-first-serve for customers needing predictable throughput. Engineering has autoscaling primitives, but there is limited automation tying intake decisions to autoscale profiles and financial accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form with enumerated commitment types (Burst, Sustained, Reserved) and machine-readable fields deployed in self-serve portal
Approval automation for standard profiles (<=X GPUs, <Y sustained RPS) that completes within 24 hours without manual ops intervention
Automated assignment of autoscale policy (ramp_up, steady_capacity, fallback) based on intake fields and workload signature
Instrumented decommit-path policy with 3-stage notifications (email, console alert, automatic decommit) and documented escalation
Dashboard tile showing active smart-contracts, utilization vs committed throughput, and projected cost delta
decisions: Adopt machine-readable commitment schema v1 (fields: commitment_type, min_throughput, burst_budget, start_window, duration_days, priority_tier)
Standard profiles will be auto-approved up to 8x burst and 2x sustained of baseline with cost caveat flags
Non-standard or high-risk requests route to Operations review; ops run a quick capacity sim runbook
tradeoffs: Automating approvals for standard profiles reduces cycle time but risks underestimating noisy tenants. We'll mitigate with conservative defaults (lower initial commit) and a mandatory 14-day probation where autoscale buffers are monitored and contracts can be adjusted.
implementation_notes: Engineering to expose an intake API endpoint (POST /reservations) that returns a commitment token. Autoscaling policies map keys to kernel scheduling presets. Billing team will ingest commitment tokens for allocation. See PRs and design artifacts linked below.
